activities.caption: each strand supplies a different thing
activities.name: styStrandMatch

config.prompt: The develop-stage loop — match each strand to what it supplies:

pairs.right: evidence of the world as you see it — observational drawing, photography, samples
made when the three start answering each other — through you

config.why: Copied research that ends with the copy scores as description, not development — the connection has to run through you, and the worked habit is three sentences: what I took, what I rejected, what it made me try.

activities.caption: from imitation to a position, in order
activities.name: styGapOrder

config.prompt: The classical apprenticeship, assembled in order:
items: The copy is never perfect: the gap between master and copy appears
Style is the shape of your deviations, accumulated and chosen
Synthesise five masters instead of one — Degas into Toulouse-Lautrec into Picasso — and imitation becomes a position
config.why: Projects over fragments: a sustained inquiry holds everything else constant, so the choices that change are visibly yours — documentation of the turnings and comparative annotation carry the rest.

activities.caption: the teacher notices the resemblance — what now?
activities.name: styInfBranch

config.root: Your portfolio's still lifes look unmistakably like your favourite painter's. A teacher raises it in a tutorial.

choices.label: Conceal the debt — vary the surface so nobody notices
choices.feedback: Denial leaves the debt unexamined and therefore generic — the resemblance stays but the thinking never happens.

choices.label: Name the inheritance, then show exactly where you deviate
choices.feedback: The deviation is the personal contribution: naming it converts an embarrassment into an argument.

choices.label: Drop the painter entirely and start from zero
choices.feedback: Every serious artist is legible as a node in a chain — severing the chain discards the vocabulary you are still learning from.

conceal.text: Unexamined resemblance is how work ends up generic — the chain of inheritance runs whether you acknowledge it or not.

name.text: The annotated page — 'taken from X, deviated here, because' — is development, not derivation.

drop.text: Erasure is not independence: you would rebuild the same vocabulary more slowly, with less honesty on the page.

config.why: The expert move is the opposite of concealment: name the inheritance, show where you deviate — knowingly produced difference is style.

activities.anchor: a standard brief is thirty thumbnails
activities.caption: bet the thumbnail brief
activities.name: styThumbEst

config.prompt: For one subject, the standard thumbnail brief asks for how many small compositional sketches in total?
config.why: Thirty — ten in landscape, ten in portrait, ten deliberately breaking your first instinct: extreme close-up, bird's-eye, negative-space-led, off-centre focal point, reversed value structure.
config.context: 10 + 10 + 10 — and the output is never the sketches themselves but the informed choice

config.text: Weak reflection says 'I could improve my shading'. Strong reflection is %%0%% — it names the specific strength and weakness %%1%%, and pairs the weakness with a %%2%%: flatten background values to within three steps of each other.
config.hint: The fix must be checkable — 'three steps of each other' checkable.

activities.anchor: diagnosing at the level where a fix is possible
activities.caption: one line of this reflection page is not reflection
activities.name: styPageSpot

config.prompt: One line of this reflection page is not reflection — click it:
lines: Strength: the diagonal of the table edge leads the eye to the focal point within two seconds — kept.
Weakness: hands read flat because I am drawing the outline instead of the planes.
Modification: next study, block in three values per hand before any contour.
Also noted: I feel bad about my hands and will try harder next time.
Marginal note, dated alongside the work, so the reasoning survives the week.
config.correction: 'I feel bad and will try harder' is a mood, not a plan — a named cause plus a checkable change is what turns commentary into development.
config.why: The connection between identified weakness and attempted modification is the visible difference between thirty pages and thirty pages of thinking.

config.prompt: Experienced practitioners routinely cut what percentage of a body of work at final selection? Place the midpoint of the routine range:
config.why: 20–40% goes — and the removed material is not failure; what distinguishes the expert is that everything cut was cut for a reason the artist could state. The passes: belonging, then quality, then sequence and rhythm.

activities.anchor: it took a lifetime to paint like a child
activities.caption: style as logo vs style as living language
activities.name: styLogoCompare

config.prompt: Two ways to hold a recognisable voice — drag the divider:

before.label: the logo
before.text: stamping the same sentence — the signature-trapped illustrator repeating 2007's hit, continuity purchased at the price of development

after.label: the living language
after.text: speaking new sentences in a recognisable voice — Picasso's stylistic leaps within a coherent intelligence, constraints keeping the variation legible

config.why: Galleries and collectors buy continuity, which creates the central tension — and premature style, built before fundamentals, calcifies into a gimmick.
